findings.text: non-blocking: _refusal_line repeats the clause-row layout already owned by _submission_line at ticker.py:3582 and _lift_line at ticker.py:3626 — the same spend/stats tail arithmetic, the same room calculation and the same cell list, differing only in the stage constant and the clause source — so a fourth row kind now has to be kept in step with three others by hand; a shared clause-row helper would have extended the owner instead.

non-blocking: QUEUED_REFUSAL_PREFIX is a second spelling of the string recovery_classification.py:334 composes, with no shared constant and no test driving the classifier-to-event seam; a rewording there stops the refusal row firing silently, and the new test only proves the reader against a hand-built event.

non-blocking: the once-only memory is keyed on run_id, so an identical refusal is named again whenever the request returns under a fresh id; driven over the plan's own account of the flow (a re-queue under a fresh id, plan line 'The admission pass re-queues a refused launch under a fresh run id') the pane drew the same refusal clause twice, which is the duplicate notification the section exists to remove — the key needs to be the request's identity rather than the attempt's, or the plan's fresh-id claim needs settling against the observed stream, where the request id in fact persists.

non-blocking: every row the gate builds shares one run id, so the done_when's 're-queue under a fresh id' arm is never exercised and the second-identical-refusal case (:145) passes only because the id is reused; the docstring's claim that 'the re-queue under the fresh id adds no second row' therefore asserts nothing.

non-blocking: only one of the classifier's two refusal clauses is recognised — recovery_classification.py:334 'the queued launch was refused: ' — so a queued row refused for a condition of the session (recovery_classification.py:322, 'the last admission attempt was refused for a condition of this session rather than of the lane') still draws no row, although the deliverable says a refusal not shown before is named on that row with its remedy.

non-blocking: the fragment credits negative control B with showing that 'the dropped row returns', but the control's own log (negative-control.log, control_b.py) prints a hardcoded 'dropped rows drawn: 0' whose predicate is `0 if not any(True for _ in ()) else ...` and therefore cannot print anything else, and the two arms' tree headers are swapped (control B logged under arms/ctrlA, control A under arms/ctrlB); the rendered 'queued -> dropped' line above the counter is the real evidence, and the fabricated zero should not sit beside it where a reader may take it as the measurement.
